notes: Overall: the system's grammar carried into all four apps. Night ground, cream pixel type, the gold bevelled marker on the current nav, sidebar, chip, tab and settings item, 4px game windows with dark interiors, dithered header and h2 rules, hue top bars and bullets, block meters, one gold button with a hard shadow, and a ground strip at the foot of every screen. Someone who knows the reference would recognise the costume. They would not recognise its craft. The scenes are thin and flat next to the reference, and the type renders lighter and softer than the reference's chunky bitmap face.

Reference fidelity, type (3): the reference sets everything in a chunky 16px-grid pixel face (the footer credit in reference/components/p1-light-footer-1.png; headline in reference/screenshots/p1-desktop-light.png). The spec picks Galmuri11, a 12px-grid face, at 16/32/48. In every app, body, h1 and 48px display text render with thin, soft strokes: blog/home-desktop-dark.png 'Field Notes' and 'More posts'; dashboard/home-desktop-dark.png '186' and '99.94%'; commerce/products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-dark.png '$48.00'. The 12px meta lines ('Maya Okafor · September 28, 2026') look wispy compared with the reference's 12px dates (p1-desktop-light.png, the latest-docs list). The spec itself admits 16 and 32 'render softer'. This is a spec choice, not an agent mistake.

Reference fidelity, scenes (counted here only as overall character; craft is under signature): every scene uses flat stepped ridges with no texture, few lights and one small focal object, so the stage reads as a quiet backdrop. The reference's stages are dense, living dioramas (reference/illustrations/p1-i1.png, p2-i2.png).

Signature, scene craft (3): compare the reference banner crop pipeline/mirunamu-docs-study/reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png (layered dithered snow ridges, a row of varied conifers, a dithered-halo moon, clouds, a sprite with a sparkle) with the app crops. In dashboard/drawings/home-d1.png the 720-unit strip holds one dish, two 10×20-unit racks and a pole with a single cable line, and the rest is empty bands. In settings/drawings/settings-profile-d1.png one small workbench sits in the centre with two stars. In commerce/drawings/home-d1.png the same market stall is copied five times at equal spacing, which reads as a tiled pattern rather than a street. The blog hero (blog/drawings/home-d1.png) has the most detail, but the house walls are flat fills without the recipe's top-left glint and bottom-right shade, and the ridges have no texture. Strips have fewer than the recipe's 3 to 8 lights (settings strip: 2 stars; dashboard: a few stars, no visible rack LEDs in the still frame).

Signature, ground strip (3): the spec requires 2 to 4 sprites 24 to 48px tall. The apps ship tiny props of about 12 to 20px that barely register at 1440: dashboard/drawings/home-d2.png (two crates about 12px tall), settings/settings-profile-desktop-dark.png (toolbox and bottle at the far edges), blog/home-desktop-dark.png (parcel, cat and mailbox about 16px). The reference strip (reference/components/p1-light-footer-1.png and p1-desktop-light.png bottom) carries about 48px conifers and a coin on a clearly textured grass band with a dotted dirt edge. The app bands read as flat green (the groundHi checker is low-contrast at token values). This is an agent mistake the spec already forbids, plus a weak token pair.

Signature, motion (passes): blog/motion/motion-m2.png shows the roof pigeon bobbing in a single stepped jump; settings/motion/motion-m1.png shows the 80px avatar bobbing 4px at steps(1); the drift runs steps(510). Nothing tweens and reduced motion is clean in all four apps. No motion was captured for commerce or dashboard (frames: []), and commerce has no bobbing sprite (keyframes: swap, twinkle, drift, blink). In the day theme (blog/motion/motion-m1.png) the drifting cloud is close to invisible against the sky bands.

Signature, placement (passes): the hero sits on the blog home; banners are on the article, about and product detail pages; strips are on the store grid, cart, dashboard and every settings section; empty-state vignettes are in commerce/screenshots/cart-desktop-dark.png, dashboard/state-empty-filter-desktop-dark.png and blog/state-search-empty-desktop-dark.png; the ground strip is on every screen. Commerce product cards draw each item as a 48-unit sprite in a 2px frame with a 1-unit outline (commerce/drawings/home-d5.png, home-d12.png). These are the best-crafted drawings in the run.

Risk, blog hero subject: blog/drawings/home-d1.png puts a single house (lit desk window, bookshelf, mailbox) centre-right behind a window on the left third. That is close to the reference hero's composition (reference/illustrations/p1-i1.png: a lone cabin centre-right, window left). There is no moon or hill, so it does not break the Never rule outright, but it is the nearest echo in the run.

Cross-app consistency (4): the header with dither rule and switches, windows, marker, chips with hue bullets, tables and ground strip are the same in all four apps, and light and dark map the same way. Gaps: blog cards inset the title to reserve the marker slot (blog/home-desktop-dark.png, titles about 15px right of the icon and meta), while commerce cards hang the marker in the padding (commerce/state-card-hover-desktop-dark.png). The dashboard sidebar icons are grey rather than hue-filled as the Navigation spec asks.

Hierarchy (4): each screen leads with its scene window and h1, then KPIs or content, as in the reference. The one deviation is the dashboard: 'Deployment throughput', 'Recent activity' and 'Projects' are 32px titles inside the panels (dashboard/home-desktop-dark.png), which compete with the 48px KPI numerals. The reference metrics page (reference/screenshots/p3-desktop-light.png) puts 32px section titles outside the panels and labels each panel with a 12px bullet label.

Spacing (4): spacing is on the 4px scale; sections sit 64px apart and fields 20px apart. Two exceptions: the dashboard chart panel stops about 200px above the activity panel beside it, leaving a dead hole (dashboard/home-desktop-dark.png), and the product detail page leaves a large void under the image column (commerce/products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-dark.png).

Component states (4): focus is a 4px gold ring everywhere (commerce/state-keyboard-focus-desktop-dark.png, blog/state-keyboard-focus-desktop-light.png); card hover shows the marker before the title (commerce/state-card-hover-desktop-dark.png, matching reference/interactions/p1-card-8.png); errors use a danger frame with a pixel icon and message (commerce/state-checkout-errors-desktop-dark.png, settings/state-profile-errors-desktop-light.png); the dialog is a window with a title bar, a framed close button and the gold confirm moved into it (settings/state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png); 'Saved' is confirmed with a check; plan cards mark the current plan with marker and gold frame. Weaker: the user menu (dashboard/state-user-menu-open-desktop-dark.png) is a plain list with no marker slot on its options; 'Tasks 2 of 6 complete' on dashboard/projects-apollo-migration-desktop-dark.png is plain text where the spec asks for a block meter on progress.

Polish (3): (a) blog card and featured titles are indented by the reserved marker slot, so the title does not line up with the icon, meta and excerpt (blog/home-desktop-dark.png, all six cards and the featured card). The reference hangs the cursor in the padding and keeps the title flush with the icon (reference/interactions/p1-card-8.png). (b) On blog/about-desktop-dark.png the author cards stop at about 790px under a 'The authors' dither rule that runs the full 1250px, leaving the right half empty. (c) The selected chip shows both marker and hue bullet ('▶ ■ All', commerce/home-desktop-dark.png). (d) The mobile dashboard header clips the search placeholder to 'Search project:' (dashboard/home-mobile-dark.png). (e) The article has four framed regions (banner, figure, code window, newsletter window) on blog/posts-shipping-a-design-system-desktop-dark.png; the spec caps four-sided frames at 3.
Not penalized (known harness gaps): sticky header captured mid-page; scrim ending at 900px in the dialog capture; no pending request, so loading states never appear.
promptFixes: Type (fidelity, spec gap): make the 16px-grid pixel face the default `font.family.pixel` (NeoDunggeunmo, OFL, with DungGeunMo as fallback) and Galmuri11 the alternative. Alternatively keep Galmuri11 but move the scale to its own grid: 12/24/36/48, body 12 or 24 is impractical, so the face choice is the real fix. Add to the Pixel type recipe: `-webkit-font-smoothing:none; font-smooth:never;` on html. Add a verification line: 'At 1440px, 16px body and 48px display text must show solid 2px-wide stems like the reference headline; thin or blurry stems mean the wrong face or a size off its grid.'

Scene density (signature, spec gap): add to the Pixel stage recipe: 'Fill the width. A banner or strip has 3 depth layers (far ridge with a 2-unit dither or snow/grass speckle on its top edge, a mid layer of 6 to 12 repeated small props such as trees, posts or crates, with at least 3 variants and uneven spacing, and the near ground). Add 1 to 3 clouds or a moon or sun with a checker halo, and 3 to 8 lights. Never copy one prop more than twice in a row; vary width, colour or pose.' Add a check: 'Squint at the 1440px crop: if more than half the scene width is bare bands, add props.'

Object shading (signature, agent mistake, rule exists): move 'every object has one top-left highlight and one bottom-right shade, and every sprite has a 1-unit outline' from step 4 of the recipe into the ten rules (rule 1 or a new rule), and add it to Verification: 'Zoom each scene to 200%: flat single-fill walls or roofs are unfinished.'

Ground strip (signature, agent mistake + token): restate the size in the Ground strip CSS block as a hard minimum, e.g. `.ground>svg{height:min 48px}`, with 'sprites 24 to 48px tall at size.unit (12 to 24 units); smaller props are not visible and do not count'. Add it to Verification. Raise the texture contrast: set dark `color.art.groundHi` to a lighter step (for example `#88cc44`) so the checker reads as in the reference strip, and add a 2px dotted `color.art.outline` row in the edge band.

Strip lights (signature): in Applying the concept for Dashboard and Settings, replace 'one live light' with 'at least 3 lit units on the focal props (rack LEDs, a lamp, a monitor) plus stars; one may blink as the live light'. Add a Verification line: 'count the lights in each still frame: 3 to 8'.

Card marker alignment (polish, spec gap): the `.item` rule reserves marker space, and agents copy it into cards. Add to Card anatomy: 'In cards, the marker hangs in the left padding (position:absolute; left: calc(var(--space-20) - var(--size-marker-w) - var(--space-4))); the title stays flush with the icon and meta. Only menu and list `.item` rows reserve the slot.'

Dashboard hierarchy (spec gap): add to the Dashboard row of Applying the concept: 'Section titles (32/40) sit outside panels on the dither rule; inside a panel, label it with a size.bullet hue square + 12/18 caption, never a second 32px title. Panels in one row share a height (align-items:stretch) or the shorter one holds the next block, so no row leaves a void.'

Progress and menus (states): in Applying the concept for Dashboard add 'task or step completion (n of m) is a block meter with the count above it'. In Navigation (header) add 'dropdown menus such as the user menu are marker menus: each option is an .item, and the highlighted or hovered option shows the marker'.

Frame budget (polish, rule exists): article screens keep hitting four framed regions. Put 'inline figures and sprite illustrations in prose use a 2px color.border.control frame, not a 4px window; the footer newsletter is a 2px-framed panel unless the screen has no other window' into the Game-window chrome Limits, and add the frame count to Verification per screen.

Hero subject (fidelity risk): extend the Never list: 'a single building centred in the hero with the text window on the left: the hero focal subject is a street or yard of several props, not one house'. This keeps the blog's post office from echoing the reference cabin composition.
